title: Plastics
examples: Can you show me an example of a polymer?
Why are some plastics harder to recycle than others?
What does the recycling number on plastic mean?

explain.say: Today we are learning about plastics and what makes them special.
Plastics are made from large molecules called polymers.
A polymer is just many small units called monomers joined together.
These long chains of polymers are why plastics last for so long.
The numbers on plastic items tell us how to recycle them.
In everyday life, think about your lunch containers.

faq.q: What is the difference between a monomer and a polymer?
faq.a: A monomer is a single, small molecule. A polymer is formed when many of these monomers link together in a long chain.
asks: Can you explain the building blocks of plastic?

faq.q: Why are plastics so durable and hard to break?
faq.a: Their durability comes from the long, strong chemical bonds within the polymer chains. These bonds require a lot of energy to break apart.

faq.q: What does the recycling code number mean?
faq.a: The number tells us the general type of plastic material used. Some codes are more commonly accepted for recycling than others.
No, not all plastics are easily recyclable in every area. The type of polymer matters a lot for recycling methods.
asks: What plastics are difficult to recycle?

faq.q: What are some common examples of polymers?
faq.a: Common examples include PET, which is often used for drink bottles, and HDPE, used for milk jugs.
asks: What is another example of a polymer?

facts: Plastics are synthetic materials made from polymers.
Polymers are formed by joining many small units called monomers.
The recycling codes help identify the type of plastic material.
PET plastic is commonly used for beverage bottles.

quiz.say: If a plastic item has the code 1, it is most likely made from:
quiz.why: Code 1 specifically identifies PET, which is commonly used for clear drink bottles.

wrong.0: PS is code 6, which is often used for packaging like Styrofoam.
wrong.2: HDPE is code 2, which is used for milk jugs, not code 1.
wrong.3: PVC is code 3, and it is used for things like pipes.

quiz.say: What is the process of linking monomers together to make a long chain called?
quiz.why: Polymerization is the scientific term for building large polymers from many small monomers.

wrong.1: Condensation is a chemical reaction, but polymerization is the specific term for forming long chains.
wrong.2: Dissolving is when something mixes in a liquid, not when molecules link up.
wrong.3: Bonding is a general term; polymerization describes the specific process of chain growth.

quiz.say: A plastic jug for milk, which is often code 2, is an example of:
quiz.why: Code 2 is the recognized code for HDPE, which is suitable for rigid containers like milk jugs.

wrong.0: PS is code 6, and it is typically used for foam packaging.
wrong.2: PET is code 1 and is usually used for clear drinks.
wrong.3: PVC is code 3 and is more often associated with plumbing materials.
